findings.title: Adapter config written with echo of interpolated secret
findings.impact: `${{ secrets.X }}` is expanded directly into the shell script. JSON containing double quotes ends the shell string early, and `$`, backticks or newlines are interpreted by the shell. The config file is therefore likely corrupted, and a crafted secret could run shell commands. `echo` may also alter backslashes. The adapter config then fails to parse.
findings.recommendation: Pass the secret through `env:` (`TRIVIEW_ADAPTER_CONFIG: ${{ secrets.TRIVIEW_ADAPTER_CONFIG }}`) and write it with `printf '%s' "$TRIVIEW_ADAPTER_CONFIG" > ...`.

findings.title: Script entrypoint check breaks for relative paths or Windows paths
findings.impact: `new URL(`file://${process.argv[1]}`)` does not percent-encode special characters such as spaces or `#`, and it fails on Windows paths. The CLI may then silently do nothing, and the workflow would write an empty request.json.

findings.title: Template's default adapter wiring is not runnable and conflicts with the README
findings.impact: The run step hard-codes a placeholder adapter path, `node_modules/triview-compass/path/to/your-adapter.js`, and the policy name `anthropic-claude-code`. The README says the Claude Code adapter needs separate config-dir wiring. The README also says `policy.json` ships in this directory, but its path and the `.triview/policy.json` path the workflow expects differ, with no copy step. Adopters get an undocumented failure, though the TODOs partly disclose this.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit TODO marker on the run step. Also state in the README that `policy.json` must be copied to `.triview/policy.json`.

findings.title: Untrusted PR code and secrets on pull_request, secret echoed into shell via expression interpolation
findings.impact: The secret is interpolated directly into the shell script via ${{ }}. Any quote, backtick or $( in the secret value breaks the script or injects shell commands. Multi-line JSON may also be mangled. The expanded value can appear in the generated script, and GitHub's masking is unreliable for transformed values. The workflow also checks out and reviews PR content, and the adapter module is loaded from the installed package. A PR author can modify .triview/policy.json in the checked-out head, so the policy, which controls data handling and provider selection, comes from untrusted PR content.

findings.title: Policy loaded from PR-controlled checkout and review output posted verbatim
findings.impact: The policy path .triview/policy.json is read from the checked-out PR head, so a PR author can alter budgets, path exclusions, secret scanning settings, or dataPolicy for the run. Model output is also posted as a PR comment inside a fenced code block. Output containing triple backticks can break out of the fence and inject markdown, links, or @mentions. The risk is moderate and the output is advisory.

findings.title: Actions pinned to mutable tags and unpinned install placeholder
findings.impact: actions/checkout@v4, setup-node@v4 and github-script@v7 are mutable tags. The job holds pull-requests:write and a model credential secret, so a compromised tag could exfiltrate the secret. The install step also uses a git URL with a placeholder, which an adopter may leave unpinned.
